title: Codex Versus Codex Speed Test
script: I raced two available Codex configurations on the exact same task. Add CSV export to this table. Handle quotes, commas, and newlines. Keep the existing tests passing. Both runs get clean copies. The clock stops only when the result passes the checks. A quick answer that exports a broken file does not win. [RUN_A_TIME_AND_RESULT]. [RUN_B_TIME_AND_RESULT]. [REPEATED_RUN_VARIATION]. [TASK_SPECIFIC_CONCLUSION]. What should I race next?
timingStatus: Estimated silent editorial timings. Refit scenes and caption timestamps to the unchanged voice-over when supplied.
concept: Same CSV-export task on clean copies; measure complete work rather than token speed.
whyNow: AI coding and automation promises are judged by a reproducible useful task.
viewerGoal: Understand what the system actually completed and where supervision matters.
hooks: I raced two available Codex configurations on the exact same task.
A fast answer is not a working CSV export.
The clock stops when the file passes, not when the AI stops.
strongestHook: I raced two available Codex configurations on the exact same task.
directorBrief: Direct this as an observable challenge: Same CSV-export task on clean copies; measure complete work rather than token speed. The viewer must see the starting problem, the exact constraint, one revealing action and the independently checked output. Let the real failure or correction create the turn. Save every first attempt. Completion claims alone never establish a result.
effort: 15–60 minutes core build/test; allow additional audit/edit time.
protocol: Use two configurations actually available to the operator; record model, effort and any supported speed option. Same clean table app and same CSV-export prompt. Acceptance: header order, commas, quotes, embedded newlines, empty cells, Unicode and existing tests. Time submission to independently verified completion. Alternate order across three paired runs when feasible and report median/range. If only one pair is recorded, call it one observed comparison; no generalized speed ratio.
evidenceRequirements: Confirm tier availability; use real timers and compare quality.
thumbnailDirection: Use the opening object or strongest real evidence crop. Put “Same Task Two Runs” in the top-middle safe area; one accent, no extra subheading.
instagramCaption: Codex Versus Codex Speed Test. Same CSV-export task on clean copies; measure complete work rather than token speed. Full test conditions and limitations belong beside the final result. [TASK_SPECIFIC_CONCLUSION]. What should I race next?
tiktokCaption: Codex Versus Codex Speed Test. WHAT SHOULD I RACE?
music: Original/licensed light percussive electronic bed, 100–115 BPM; leave real clicks readable. No music asset is included.
recordings: Full continuous source run plus selected genuine action clips. Record 1080p or higher, readable UI, cursor, exact OS/tool/plan and run clock. Keep uncropped originals.
screenshots: Baseline, first attempt, final output, official license/plan/version, and each verdict evidence frame. Synthetic fixtures only.
icons: Use original vector shapes and existing studio-kit Icon components; use official product marks only for identification. No random decorative icon grid.
assetBrief: Two runs, task, export, passing tests.
